Hi Rishi,

Thanks for sending the updated Order Form. Finance circled back — they are okay with splitting the first-year commit into tranches but need clarity on: which legal entity will receive invoices, whether we can get a W-9 (US entity) or VAT registration (if invoicing EU entity), and an explicit schedule for invoice milestones tied to commits.

Two specifics:
- They want the first 30% invoiced on signature, 40% at activation, 30% at the 6-month mark.
- If invoices are issued to Acme Global (non-US), they will require VAT documentation; otherwise for Acme Inc (US) they need a W-9.

Can you confirm the approved invoicing entity and whether Redwood can accept this tranche split? Also loop in your legal for any billing-side redlines.

Best,
Lisa

Subject: Re: Order Form v3 — payment cadence question

Hi Lisa — thanks, that helps.

Short answers up front:
- Payment tranche split is reasonable from a commercial perspective — we can support 30/40/30 as long as the Order Form ties each tranche to a deliverable (signature, activation, 6-month anniversary).
- Invoicing entity: Redwood typically invoices Redwood Inference, Inc. (US). If you require invoicing to Acme Global, we need to confirm tax residency and may need to issue to the international subsidiary — that requires Legal sign-off and a VAT certificate from Acme.

I’m looping in Ben (payments) and Kimberly (legal/compliance) to confirm redline tolerance and required evidence. I’ll also attach our suggested redlines to the Order Form (see attached v3 with line-by-line comments).

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly confirms whether Redwood can accept alternate invoicing entity and any systems/PO impacts.
2) If Acme prefers an alternate entity, Mark (your counsel) and Kimberly to coordinate a short addendum on invoicing & tax evidence.
3) Ben will confirm that our billing system can produce the three invoices on the requested schedule and deliver PO/ESP mapping.

Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Turner <lisa.turner@acmecorp.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Coleman <m.coleman@morganreed.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-10T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form v3 — payment cadence question

Thanks for the context. A few legal points from Redwood’s side to make the invoice-entity switch workable: 

1) Contracting entity: Our standard MSA binds Redwood Inference, Inc. We can accept invoices to an Acme entity other than the one in the billing block only if Acme (a) confirms legal ability to pay on behalf of that entity, and (b) provides tax residency evidence (W-9 for US entity; VAT reg / local tax certificate for non-US). Please provide the exact legal name and tax ID of the Acme entity to be invoiced.

2) Payment terms: Net-45 is fine, but in the Order Form we need explicit language tying payment triggers to your acceptance criteria and to the tranche milestones (signature/activation/6-month). We should avoid open-ended language like "invoice on commencement" — instead specify dates or defined events.

3) Withholdings & taxes: If Acme is outside the US, Redwood may be subject to withholding per local tax law; we will pass through tax-related charges as required. For US invoicing, a completed W-9 will avoid US backup withholding.

4) PO/Invoice routing: Please confirm the email and AP contact for invoice submission and whether PO numbers will be present on the invoice. If you require electronic invoicing (EDI/Ariba), we’ll need that format flagged.

We propose the following edits in the attached redline: add explicit invoicing entity field, define tranche milestones, require tax evidence within 10 business days of execution, and include a clause stating Redwood will not be obligated to change the invoicing entity retroactively without a signed addendum.

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Mark Coleman <m.coleman@morganreed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lisa Turner <lisa.turner@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form v3 — payment cadence question

Kimberly / Rishi — thanks for the clear notes. Acme legal confirms they can provide a VAT registration for Acme Global and will supply the W-9 for Acme Inc if the invoice goes to the US entity. One governance note: Acme prefers the first invoice to be "on execution" not "on signature" — our processes treat execution = countersign by both parties.

I attach Acme’s procurement contact list and a short statement of intent to invoice to Acme Global pending VAT evidence (attached). We can accept the "no retroactive entity change" clause so long as Acme can nominate an invoicing entity on signature and provide the required tax docs within 10 business days.

Mark
Morgan & Reed LLP (counsel to Acme)

Quick ops check from Billing: we can implement the 30/40/30 tranche schedule and tie invoices to these events: (1) execution (invoice #1), (2) activation of dedicated environment / API keys (invoice #2), (3) 6-month anniversary of activation (invoice #3). Two asks from accounting:

- Please confirm whether Acme will provide a single PO that covers all tranches or separate POs per invoice. Our system can accept either, but PO presence helps match.
- Confirm AP email and whether they require PDF invoices only or an invoice XML (if so we’ll need the schema).

Operationally we will hold the first invoice until we receive the PO/PO number (if Acme requires). If tax evidence is delayed beyond 10 business days, we will still issue the invoice but note tax withholding may be applied per local law (pass-through).

If everyone is aligned I’ll prepare the billing instructions we can include in the Order Form (Billing Appendix) and push a final redline to the doc.

Thanks — Ben
Director, Billing & Revenue Ops
